claim: EY's report on Web Summit's economic impact was released on 5 November.
EY's report puts Web Summit's total impact on Portugal at 2,492 million euros over ten editions.
Net of hosting costs, Web Summit gives Portugal a benefit of more than 230 million euros a year.
Portugal's startups grew from 2,193 in 2016 to 5,091 in 2025, an increase of 132%.
Web Summit's ten editions drew more than 683,000 participants.
Taxes paid in Portugal because of Web Summit were 25 million euros in 2016 and 50.7 million euros in 2025.
Participants' spending on lodging, food, transport and shops totalled 730 million euros, with a peak of 118 million euros in 2025.
Web Summit sustains more than 3,000 full-time jobs.
The 191 companies in the 2024 startup programme raised 607.5 million euros together.
A November 2021 Ministry of Economy evaluation found the 2016 to 2019 editions' gross value added was 196 million euros lower than estimated.
